theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A national association of small hoteliers asks you to plan its first two-day conference in Ocho Rios. What should you agree with the organising committee before anything else?
options: The colour scheme and theme for the stage
The menu for the opening night dinner
The purpose, audience and measurable aims
The names of the speakers for each session

questions.stem: Which feature most clearly makes an event a conference rather than an ordinary business meeting?
options: Many delegates from several bodies follow a planned programme
A chairperson keeps order and the minutes are approved later
A small team meets to decide actions for its own department
An agenda and papers are sent out a few days before people meet

questions.stem: A ministry is planning a regional conference with a steering committee and several sub-committees. What is the main benefit of giving each sub-committee written terms of reference?
options: It removes the need for a conference manager to oversee the work
It allows each sub-committee to spend money without approval
It means the steering committee no longer has to meet at all
Each group knows its tasks, limits, budget and reporting line

questions.stem: Planning for a 500-delegate conference in Montego Bay starts twelve months ahead. Why is the venue usually booked so early?
options: Venues will not give a price less than a year before an event
Large venues are scarce, and the date and place shape every other plan
Speakers will only agree to come once the full hotel bill has been paid
Delegates need the venue's name before they can renew passports

questions.stem: A conference has fixed costs of J$2,400,000. Each delegate costs J$9,000 for meals and materials, and the fee is J$25,000. How many paying delegates are needed to break even?
Which conference cost is usually variable, rising with the number of delegates?
options: Hire of the main hall for both days of the event
The keynote speaker's agreed fee
Lunch and coffee breaks for each delegate
Design of the conference website

questions.stem: A conference budget totals J$5,600,000 and the committee sets a 10% contingency on that total. How much should be held back?
A bank offers to sponsor a business conference in return for its logo on all materials. What should the conference manager do before accepting?
options: Accept at once, because any sponsorship lowers the delegate fee
Ask the bank to choose the keynote speakers as part of the deal
Keep the sponsorship from delegates to avoid any complaints
Check fit with the aims, agree benefits in writing, look for conflicts

questions.stem: Which question matters most when choosing between two hotels for a residential conference of 250 delegates?
options: Which hotel has the newer logo and website
Which hotel the chairman stayed at last year
Which hotel is closest to the organiser's home
Which hotel has the rooms, space and access needed

questions.stem: Before signing a venue contract, why should the conference manager make a site inspection?
options: To check rooms, access, sound and services match what was promised
To meet the hotel's other guests and invite them to attend
To collect free samples of the menus for the whole committee to taste
To agree the delegate fee with the hotel's front desk staff

questions.stem: A hotel contract has a block of 80 rooms for two nights at J$18,000 a night, and lets the group fall 20% below the block without charge. Only 55 rooms are taken up. What does the group owe for unused rooms?
Which clause in a venue contract sets what the organiser pays if it calls the conference off at different times before the date?
options: The force majeure clause
The cancellation clause
The attrition clause
The indemnity clause

questions.stem: A venue asks for the final number of lunches 72 hours before the conference. What does this guarantee usually mean for the organiser?
options: The organiser pays for at least that number, even if fewer attend
The venue must give a refund for any delegate who leaves early
The venue may serve fewer meals if some delegates arrive late
The organiser can still change the number freely on the morning itself

questions.stem: A workshop needs 120 delegates to work in small groups while still seeing the stage and screen. Which room layout suits it best?
options: Theatre
Boardroom
Classroom
Cabaret

questions.stem: Delegates at last year's conference said the programme was 'all talk and no time to meet people'. Which change best answers this?
options: Add two more keynote speeches to each morning
Shorten lunch so more sessions can fit in
Build in longer breaks, networking and workshops
Print the speakers' slides in the delegate pack

questions.stem: In a conference programme, what is a breakout session?
options: The main session that all delegates attend together in the hall
A smaller session held alongside others, on a narrower topic
A break for coffee between the morning and afternoon sessions
A session at the end where the chair closes the conference

questions.stem: A guest speaker from Trinidad agrees to give the keynote. Which step best reduces the risk of problems on the day?
options: Leave travel to the speaker and meet them at the hall
Ask the speaker to bring the slides on the morning itself
Tell the speaker the exact topic once they arrive in Jamaica
Confirm topic, timing, fee, travel and slide deadline in writing

questions.stem: Why should each session chair be given a written brief before the conference?
options: So they know timings, speaker details and what to do if one is absent
So they can rewrite each of the speakers' talks to suit the audience better
So they can collect the delegate fees at the door of their room
So they can choose which delegates may ask questions at the end

questions.stem: A conference uses online registration. Which feature of the form best helps the organiser plan catering and access?
options: A box for delegates to rate last year's event
A link to the hotel's restaurant menu online
Questions on dietary needs and access needs
A list of all other delegates' phone numbers

questions.stem: Why do many conferences offer an early-bird rate?
options: To charge the latest delegates less than everyone else
To avoid having to set a budget for the event at all
To bring in cash and firm numbers early in the planning
To make sure no delegate can cancel their place later

questions.stem: Registration forms collect delegates' names, phone numbers, employers and dietary or medical notes. Which practice follows the general aims of the data protection law?
options: Sell the list to sponsors so they can contact the delegates
Collect only what is needed, keep it secure, use it for the event
Post the full list on the conference website for networking
Keep all of the data forever in case it helps with a future event

questions.stem: A conference for small business owners has few registrations six weeks before the date. What should the manager do first?
options: Find out why, by checking the message, channels, price and timing
Cancel the conference and refund the delegates who have paid
Cut the programme to a half day without telling the delegates
Double the fee so that far fewer delegates are needed to break even

questions.stem: A delegate who uses a wheelchair has registered. Which arrangement shows good planning?
options: Seat the delegate at the back so others are not disturbed
Ask the delegate to bring a helper to lift them up the steps
Give the delegate a recording instead of a seat in the hall
Check step-free access to rooms, toilets, stage and transport

questions.stem: Twenty delegates are coming from other Caribbean countries and from West Africa. What extra support should the organiser plan?
options: A separate programme held for them in another hotel
Invitation letters for visas where needed, and airport transfers
A rule that they must pay in cash in Jamaica before the event
A shorter programme so they can leave before the dinner

questions.stem: Delegates staying at three hotels must reach the venue by 8:00 a.m. Which transport plan is soundest?
options: Tell delegates to find their own way and hope they are on time
Hire one bus to make a single trip round all three hotels at 7:45
Book enough buses with set pick-up times and a contact for each
Start the programme at 10:00 so that transport does not matter

questions.stem: A conference in Negril is planned for late September. Which risk should the plan deal with most clearly?
options: A hurricane or severe weather near the date
Delegates wanting too much time at the beach
Too many vegetarian meals being ordered
Speakers bringing too many printed handouts

questions.stem: In a conference risk register, what does the organiser record for each risk?
options: Only the names of the people who might cause it
Only the cost of insurance for the whole event
The delegate list and their seat numbers in the hall
Its likelihood, impact, controls and who owns it

questions.stem: On the morning of the conference, a fire exit in the main hall is blocked by stacked exhibition boxes. What should the conference manager do?
options: Note it in the final report for the venue to fix next time
Have the boxes moved at once and keep the exit clear
Tell delegates in the opening speech to use another door
Wait until lunch, when fewer people are in the hall

questions.stem: The venue's main hall is rated for 350 people. Registrations reach 380. What is the right action?
options: Close registration at the safe limit or move to a larger room
Add extra chairs in the aisles so that everyone fits in
Let all 380 in, since some will leave the hall early
Ask the extra delegates to stand along the back wall during the talks

questions.stem: Which document tells the conference team, minute by minute, what happens on the day and who is responsible for each item?
options: The venue contract
The delegate list
The run sheet
The budget report

questions.stem: Volunteers from a Kingston college will help at the registration desk. What should happen before the conference opens?
options: They should be told to ask the delegates what to do
They should be given the master budget to read
They should be shown only where the staff canteen is
They should be briefed on tasks, contacts and emergencies

questions.stem: Long queues build at the registration desk twenty minutes before the opening. What is the best immediate response?
options: Close the desk and let delegates collect badges later
Open extra lanes, such as one for pre-paid delegates
Delay the opening by two hours until all are registered
Ask the delegates at the back of the line to come tomorrow

questions.stem: Ten minutes before her session, a speaker's laptop will not connect to the projector. What should the session manager do first?
options: Cancel the session and send the delegates to lunch
Ask the delegates to read the speaker's notes instead
Call the technician and load the backup copy of the slides
Move the speaker to the very end of the programme

questions.stem: A regional conference will be hybrid, with some delegates joining online. What is the main extra thing to plan?
options: Sound, a stable link and a host who brings online delegates in
A larger buffet for the delegates who join from their homes
A second venue where all the online delegates can meet together in person
Printed name badges posted to each of the online delegates

questions.stem: Exhibitors have paid for stands in the conference foyer. What should the organiser give them before the event?
options: The delegates' private phone numbers and e-mail addresses
The right to speak during the opening ceremony
A seat on the steering committee for the conference
A pack with the floor plan, set-up times, rules and contacts

questions.stem: Lunch for 240 delegates must include 15% vegetarian meals. How many vegetarian meals should be ordered?
The committee wants the conference to be kinder to the environment. Which step makes the biggest practical difference?
options: Print the full programme in colour for each delegate
Use an event app, water stations and local suppliers
Give every delegate a plastic bag of small gifts
Fly in all the speakers instead of using video links

questions.stem: A government agency is hiring an events company to run its national conference. What must the agency's manager do?
options: Choose the company owned by a friend because it is reliable
Split the contract into small parts to avoid the tender rules
Follow the procurement rules for public bodies and record why
Pay the company in full before the work is agreed in writing

questions.stem: A hotel offers the conference manager a free weekend for her family if she books the conference there. What should she do?
options: Accept it, as long as the hotel is also the cheapest
Decline or declare it, as the gifts policy requires
Accept it quietly, since it is a personal gift only
Tell the other hotels to make her a better offer

questions.stem: Midway through planning, catering costs are forecast to be J$400,000 over budget. What should the manager do?
options: Ignore it, as costs usually even out by the end
Take the money from the speakers' agreed fees without telling them
Ask delegates to pay extra in cash on the day of the event
Find the cause, seek savings or approval, update the forecast

questions.stem: How can the organiser best judge whether the conference met its aims?
options: Count how many delegates stayed for the closing dinner
Ask the hotel manager whether the event went well
Compare survey results, numbers and outcomes with the aims
Check how many photographs were posted on social media

questions.stem: After the conference, what should the manager do with its finances?
options: Check invoices, pay suppliers and compare actuals with the budget
Keep any surplus as a bonus for the conference team members
Throw away the receipts once the venue's bill has been paid
Wait a year before paying the smaller suppliers what they are owed

questions.stem: Which follow-up action after the conference adds most value for delegates?
options: Sending delegates the hotel's invoice for the venue
Removing the conference page from the website at once
Asking delegates to pay for the evaluation survey
Sending thanks, slides or proceedings and agreed actions

questions.stem: Why should a conference manager write a final report with lessons learned?
options: To give the venue reasons to raise its prices next year
So the next conference repeats what worked and fixes the rest
To place the blame for each problem on the volunteers
So that the budget for the next conference can be cut by half or more

questions.stem: Why might a conference organiser take out event cancellation insurance?
options: To cover losses if events beyond its control force cancellation
To guarantee that every single delegate will enjoy the full programme
To avoid having to sign any contract with the venue
To pay speakers who choose not to turn up on the day

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the name of the room layout with rows of chairs facing the stage and no tables?
What is the name of the clause in a hotel contract that sets how far the group may reduce its room block without paying a penalty?
What is the usual name for a visit to a possible venue to check its rooms and services before booking?
What one word describes a conference session that all delegates attend together?
Give the four-letter abbreviation for the part of the tourism trade made up of meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions.
A conference has fixed costs of J$1,500,000. Each delegate adds J$5,000 in variable costs and pays a fee of J$17,500. How many delegates are needed to break even?
A delegate fee of J$20,000 is cut by 15% for early registration. What is the reduced fee, in J$?
What term describes a registered delegate who neither attends nor cancels?
A conference has 320 delegates, and 12.5% of them need a gluten-free lunch. How many gluten-free lunches are needed?
A hotel allows a 10% drop below a block of 120 rooms without charge. What is the lowest number of rooms the group can take without a penalty?
What one word describes a conference where some delegates attend in person and others take part online?
What is the usual name for the space in a conference foyer that an exhibitor pays for to show its products?
What is the term for the main speaker who opens a conference with a talk that sets its theme?
Out of 260 delegates, 195 completed the evaluation survey. What was the response rate, as a percentage?
What two-word term names the contract clause that frees both sides when events outside their control, such as a hurricane, make the conference impossible?

essays.stem: A national association of small manufacturers asks you to plan a two-day conference for 300 delegates in Kingston, eight months from now. Set out your plan from today to the opening, with the main stages and timings.
essays.modelAnswer: In the first month I would agree the purpose, audience and measurable aims with the committee, such as 300 paying delegates, a satisfaction score of at least 4 out of 5 and a small surplus. I would set up sub-committees for programme, sponsorship, marketing and logistics, each with terms of reference, and draw up a draft budget with a break-even fee. By month two I would inspect and book the venue and hotel rooms, checking the contract terms on cancellation, attrition and catering guarantees. In months two to four I would confirm speakers in writing, seek sponsors and open online registration with an early-bird rate. From month four I would promote the event through members, industry media and social media, and track registrations weekly against target. In months six and seven I would confirm transport, audio-visual needs, catering numbers and accessibility, and complete the risk register. In the final month I would issue joining instructions, prepare the run sheet, brief staff and volunteers, and check every booking. A critical-path timeline would show who does what and by when.
markingPoints: Starts by agreeing purpose, audience and measurable aims, with a committee structure
Books the venue early after inspection and checks key contract terms
Plans speakers, sponsorship, registration and promotion in a sensible order
Covers logistics, access, catering numbers and a risk register
Uses a timeline with owners and dates, ending with a run sheet and briefings

essays.stem: Your committee must choose between a large all-inclusive hotel in Montego Bay and a university conference centre in Kingston for a 250-delegate professional conference. Evaluate the two options and make a justified recommendation.
essays.modelAnswer: The Montego Bay hotel offers rooms, meals and meeting space in one place, which makes logistics simple and helps networking in the evenings. It is close to the international airport, which suits overseas delegates. However, its package rate may be high, delegates may be drawn away by the beach, and room blocks often carry strict attrition and cancellation terms. The Kingston centre is likely to be cheaper, central for most local delegates and close to government offices and businesses, and it may have good lecture halls and technical support. Its weaknesses are that delegates would need separate hotels and transport, catering may be more basic and evening networking is harder to arrange. I would compare both against the conference's aims, budget, capacity, access, audio-visual quality and the delegate profile, using a weighted score after site visits. If most delegates are local professionals and cost is tight, I would recommend the Kingston centre, with a partner hotel and shuttle. If the aim is to attract regional delegates and build networks, the hotel is the better choice.
markingPoints: Identifies strengths and weaknesses of the resort hotel
Identifies strengths and weaknesses of the Kingston centre
Uses clear criteria such as aims, cost, capacity, access, transport and technical support
Suggests a fair method such as site visits and a weighted comparison
Gives a recommendation that is justified by the conference's aims and delegates

essays.stem: Explain how you would build and control the budget for a fee-paying conference, including how you would set the delegate fee.
essays.modelAnswer: I would list every expected cost and sort it into fixed costs, such as venue hire, audio-visual equipment, speakers, marketing and insurance, and variable costs per delegate, such as meals, badges, bags and printed materials. I would get written quotes for the main items and add a contingency, often around 10%, for the unexpected. I would then estimate income from sponsorship, exhibitors and delegate fees. To set the fee, I would work out the break-even number: fixed costs less sponsorship, divided by the fee less the variable cost per delegate. I would test this at realistic attendance figures, compare the fee with similar events and the members' ability to pay, and set an early-bird rate to bring in cash early. Once the budget is approved, I would record every commitment, compare actuals and forecasts with the budget each month, and report variances to the committee. Any overspend would need a cause, a saving elsewhere or approval. After the event I would reconcile all invoices and report the final surplus or deficit.
markingPoints: Lists costs and separates fixed costs from variable costs per delegate
Uses quotes and includes a contingency
Includes income from sponsors and exhibitors as well as fees
Sets the fee using break-even, market comparison and early-bird pricing
Controls the budget through commitments, monthly comparisons and approval of changes

essays.stem: Identify the main risks to a residential conference held in Jamaica during the hurricane season, and describe how you would manage them.
essays.modelAnswer: The main risks are a storm or hurricane near the date, power or internet failure, low registrations, a key speaker cancelling, a health or security incident, and a supplier failing to deliver. I would list each risk in a register, score its likelihood and impact, and name an owner and controls. For weather, I would check the venue's hurricane plan, agree clear postponement terms and a force majeure clause in the contracts, take out event cancellation insurance and set a decision date, linked to official weather warnings, for whether to go ahead. I would have a communication plan to reach every delegate quickly by e-mail and text. For power, I would confirm that the venue has a standby generator. For speakers, I would have a stand-in or a recorded talk. For health and safety, I would confirm first aid, emergency exits and capacity limits with the venue. I would review the register at each committee meeting and brief the team on the plans before the event.
markingPoints: Names several realistic risks, including weather, power, numbers, speakers and safety
Uses a risk register with likelihood, impact, owner and controls
Plans for weather through contracts, insurance and a go or no-go decision point
Plans communication with delegates and backups for key services
Reviews the risks regularly and briefs the team

essays.stem: Explain how you would design a two-day conference programme that keeps 200 delegates engaged and meets the conference's aims.
essays.modelAnswer: I would start from the aims and the delegates' needs, found through a short survey of members and last year's evaluation. I would open each day with a strong plenary, such as a keynote speaker who sets the theme, then use breakout sessions on narrower topics so delegates can choose what suits them. I would mix formats: panels, case studies from Jamaican businesses, practical workshops and short question-and-answer slots, because long lectures lose attention. Sessions would be no longer than about 60 to 90 minutes, with breaks of at least 20 minutes and a long lunch to allow networking. I would put the most demanding sessions in the morning and more active ones after lunch. I would leave time for exhibitors and for a social event in the evening. Each session would have a chair who keeps time. I would publish the programme early so delegates can plan, and finish with a closing plenary that sums up the key points and agreed actions.
markingPoints: Bases the programme on the aims and the delegates' needs
Uses plenary and breakout sessions in a sensible balance
Varies the formats and keeps sessions to a manageable length
Builds in breaks, networking and exhibitor time
Plans chairing, timing and a closing session that draws the points together

essays.stem: Describe how you would select, brief and look after speakers for a conference, from the first invitation to the follow-up.
essays.modelAnswer: I would choose speakers who match the aims and the audience, checking their knowledge, speaking skill and reputation, and aiming for a balance of voices, including local and regional experts. I would invite each one in writing with the topic, length, audience, date and any fee or expenses offered, and confirm their acceptance with an agreement. I would ask for a short biography and photograph for the programme and set a deadline for slides, so they can be checked and loaded in advance. Travel, accommodation and airport transfers would be arranged and confirmed for those who need them. Before the event I would send a speaker brief with the timetable, room layout, equipment, the session chair's name and a contact number. On the day a named team member would meet each speaker, show them the room and test their slides. After the conference I would thank each speaker in writing, share the feedback on their session and pay any fee or expenses promptly.
markingPoints: Selects speakers against the aims and audience, with balance
Confirms terms in writing, including topic, timing and fee
Collects biographies and slides in advance and arranges travel
Briefs speakers and supports them on the day
Thanks them, shares feedback and settles payments

essays.stem: Describe how you would manage a conference on the day itself, from set-up to the close.
essays.modelAnswer: I would arrive early with the run sheet and walk the venue with the venue's events manager, checking room layouts, signs, audio-visual equipment, catering times, fire exits and access. I would hold a short briefing with staff and volunteers so that each knows their task, the timings, the contact numbers and the emergency procedure. Registration would open at least an hour before the first session, with lanes for pre-paid delegates and for those still paying. During the day I would keep in touch with the team by radio or phone, keep sessions to time with the session chairs, and check catering numbers before each meal. I would deal quickly with problems, such as a missing speaker or a failed projector, using the backup plans. I would keep a log of incidents and decisions. At the close I would make sure the venue is cleared, equipment returned, lost property recorded and the takings secured. Finally I would hold a short debrief with the team while the day is fresh.
markingPoints: Checks the venue against the run sheet before delegates arrive
Briefs staff and volunteers on tasks, contacts and emergencies
Runs registration efficiently and keeps sessions and catering to time
Handles problems with backup plans and logs incidents
Closes down properly and holds a team debrief

essays.stem: A public body is planning a regional conference for officials from across the Caribbean. Compare an in-person, a fully online and a hybrid format, and recommend one.
essays.modelAnswer: An in-person conference gives the best networking and attention, and builds relationships between officials, but it is the most costly because of travel, hotels and catering, and some officials may not get approval to travel. A fully online conference is far cheaper and lets many more people take part, but attention drops, time zones and connections can be a problem, and informal networking is weak. A hybrid conference lets key officials meet in person while others join online, so reach grows without losing all the benefits of meeting. However, it is the hardest to run well: it needs good cameras and sound, a stable connection, an online host, and a way for remote delegates to ask questions so they are not treated as second-class. The cost of the technology must be budgeted. For a regional public body with limited travel budgets, I would recommend a hybrid format, with a small in-person core in Kingston and a strong online platform, provided a specialist audio-visual supplier is engaged and tested in advance.
markingPoints: Gives the benefits and drawbacks of an in-person conference
Gives the benefits and drawbacks of a fully online conference
Explains what a hybrid format needs to work well
Considers cost, reach and the needs of the public body
Makes a clear, justified recommendation

essays.stem: Explain how you would evaluate the success of a conference, and describe what you would put in the final report to the committee.
essays.modelAnswer: I would measure the conference against the aims agreed at the start. I would collect delegate feedback through a short survey, sent on the last day while the event is fresh, asking about content, speakers, venue, catering and value for money, with space for comments. I would also collect feedback from speakers, sponsors, exhibitors and the team. Hard measures would include the number of delegates against target, the no-show rate, the response rate and the final financial result against budget. I would compare these with last year's figures where they exist. The final report would include a short summary, the aims and how far each was met, attendance and survey results, the financial outturn with the main variances explained, what went well, what went wrong and why, and clear recommendations for the next conference. I would attach the budget reconciliation, the survey summary and the risk and incident log. The report would go to the committee within a few weeks and be kept for future planning.
markingPoints: Evaluates against the aims agreed at the start
Collects feedback from delegates and other groups such as sponsors and speakers
Uses measures such as attendance, response rate and financial outturn
Report covers results, variances, what worked and what did not
Gives recommendations and keeps the report for future planning

essays.stem: Explain the main terms you would check in a venue contract for a conference, and how you would manage the venue and other suppliers before and during the event.
essays.modelAnswer: Before signing, I would check the dates, rooms and times included, the price and what it covers, the deposit and payment dates, and how GCT and service charges are shown. I would look closely at the cancellation clause, with its scale of charges, the attrition clause for the room block, the deadline for catering guarantees and the force majeure clause. I would also check rules on outside suppliers, decorations, noise and insurance, and who is liable for damage. I would make sure that what was promised at the site visit is written into the contract. To manage the venue and other suppliers, such as audio-visual, transport and printers, I would name one contact for each, confirm every order in writing, keep a supplier schedule with deadlines and check progress regularly. On the day I would meet the venue's events manager at set times, check each delivery and service against the order, record any problem straight away and raise it calmly. Afterwards I would check every invoice against the agreed terms before paying.
markingPoints: Checks scope, price, payment terms and taxes
Checks cancellation, attrition, catering guarantee and force majeure terms
Checks liability, insurance and rules on outside suppliers
Manages suppliers with written orders, named contacts and a schedule
Checks services on the day and invoices before payment

practical1.title: Plan a one-day business conference: plan, budget, programme and risk register
practical1.brief: The assessor gives your group a case: a made-up professional association wants a one-day conference for 150 delegates in a Kingston or Montego Bay venue, with a budget limit, two venue quotes and a list of possible speakers. As a group, produce a conference plan for the committee. Give each member a named role: project lead (writes the aims, timeline to the day and who does what), budget officer (builds the budget in a spreadsheet with fixed and variable costs, a contingency, sponsorship income, the delegate fee and the break-even number, checking every figure twice), programme planner (writes the programme with plenary and breakout sessions, breaks and timings), venue and logistics officer (compares the two venues with a scoring table and lists catering, access and transport needs), and risk officer (writes a risk register with likelihood, impact, controls and owners). In a group of four, the project lead also writes the risk register. Finish by presenting the plan to the assessor in 10 minutes as if to the committee.
materials: Case brief with venue quotes, speaker list and budget limit from the assessor
Computers with spreadsheet and word processor software
Flipchart paper, markers and sticky notes
photos: The written aims and timeline with owners and dates
The budget spreadsheet on screen showing the break-even number
The conference programme with sessions and timings
The venue scoring table with the group's choice
The group presenting the plan to the assessor
checklist: Took a named role and completed their part of the plan
Aims are clear and measurable and the timeline has owners and dates
Budget separates fixed and variable costs and the break-even figure is correct
Programme balances plenary, breakout sessions, breaks and networking
Venue choice is justified against clear criteria, including access
Risk register covers realistic risks with controls and owners
Presented their part clearly and answered the assessor's questions
safety: Treat the case data and quotes as confidential; hand all printouts to the assessor at the end
Use made-up names only for people and suppliers
Respect each other's views and share the workload fairly
Take a short break away from the screen during the task

practical2.title: Run a simulated conference morning, handle incidents and write the evaluation
practical2.brief: Your group runs the opening morning of a short mini-conference at the Centre, with other trainees or staff as delegates. The assessor gives you a delegate list, a programme and sealed incident cards that will be handed to you during the morning (for example a late speaker, a projector failure, a delegate with an access need, a queue at registration or a fire alarm drill). Give each member a named role: conference manager (leads the team briefing and makes the decisions on the day), registration lead (sets up and runs the registration desk with badges and a check-in list), session manager (keeps the sessions to time and works with the speaker and the equipment), delegate care officer (deals with delegate needs, catering numbers and the incident log), and evaluation officer (runs a short delegate survey and writes up the results). In a group of four, the conference manager also does delegate care. Before the start, write a run sheet. Afterwards, write a one-page evaluation report with lessons learned.
materials: Delegate list, programme and incident cards from the assessor
Name badges, check-in list and signs
A projector or screen and a laptop
A short delegate survey form (paper or online)
Computer and printer for the run sheet and report
photos: The run sheet with times and named responsibilities
The team briefing before delegates arrive
The incident log with each incident and the action taken
The delegate survey results in a table or chart
checklist: Took a named role and carried it out during the morning
Run sheet covers each item with a time and a named person
Gave clear, polite help to delegates
